children: India's central bank won't be able to look entirely past the rise in inflation, UOB economists say as they pencil in two back-to-back 25bp rate hikes starting from December. Under UOB's baseline projections, headline inflation could breach the upper bound of the RBI's 2%-6% tolerance band by fiscal 3Q and remain above 6% until early 1Q. That would imply negative real rates that may necessitate tighter monetary conditions to constrain demand-driven inflation, says UOB's Jester Koh. While price pressures remain highly concentrated in the food category for now, the RBI is still likely to act given the potential influence on household inflation expectations, which have strengthened meaningfully since the start of 2026. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
